OLLI MAKINEN
Senior Signal Processing Professional | Innovation Driver | Technical Strategist

PROFESSIONAL PROFILE

Results-driven signal processing engineer with 7+ years of experience delivering cutting-edge solutions across multiple technology domains. Strong technical academic grounding with a proven ability to drive innovation from concept through to production deployment. Experienced in satellite and airborne platform engineering. Demonstrated thought leadership and cross-functional team management capabilities. Active contributor to open-source communities and technical publications.

CORE COMPETENCIES

- Signal Processing & Algorithm Development
- Satellite & Airborne Systems Engineering
- Cross-Functional Team Leadership
- End-to-End Solution Delivery
- Technical Strategy & Innovation Management
- Stakeholder Engagement & Communication
- Publication & Open-Source Contribution

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Sinikaari Optics | Signal Processing Engineer
2019 -- Present | Oulu, Finland

Finnish citizen with full work authorisation in the EU. Based in Oulu since joining Sinikaari.

- Spearheaded development of next-generation optical sensor signal processing architectures, driving significant performance improvements across the product portfolio
- Delivered high-impact signal processing solutions for diverse sensing modalities, consistently exceeding project KPIs and technical performance benchmarks
- Engaged in end-to-end product development lifecycle from requirements capture through architecture design, implementation, validation, and production handoff
- Drove continuous process improvement initiatives across the signal processing engineering function

PROJECTS

Sinikaari OptiSense Platform Enhancement (2022--2024)
- Led comprehensive signal conditioning pipeline redesign for the OptiSense product series, coordinating across hardware, software, and test engineering workstreams
- Delivered technical presentations and authored project documentation in English for Sinikaari's international customer review meetings and partner engineering workshops
- Achieved significant SNR improvement while reducing computational load on target processing hardware

EDUCATION

BTech Materials Science and Engineering
Salsette Institute of Technology Bombay
Graduated 2018

INTERESTS

Ice hockey, trail running, home automation projects
application.cover_letter_markdown:
Kaikuvaara Oy
RE: Senior Signal Processing Engineer

I believe I am the right candidate to drive Kaikuvaara's signal processing capabilities to the next level. With over seven years of hands-on experience delivering high-impact signal processing solutions at Sinikaari Optics, I have built a comprehensive technical skillset that spans the full engineering lifecycle from concept through to production deployment. I am looking for a role where I can operate at greater scale and create even larger technical impact, and the Senior Signal Processing Engineer position at Kaikuvaara fits that requirement.

Throughout my career I have maintained deep expertise across the signal processing technology stack. I bring strong capabilities in phased-array and beamforming signal processing, having developed extensive knowledge of array-based architectures and spatial processing approaches across multiple sensing modalities. My embedded DSP skills in C and C++ are well-developed and battle-tested. I also bring robust production Python capabilities that I deploy across data processing pipelines, algorithm prototyping, and production deployment automation. RF measurement is another core competency -- understanding the complete signal chain from antenna through to digital output is something I consider fundamental for any serious signal processing engineer, not optional.

What differentiates my profile is the combination of deep technical depth with consistent delivery execution. I don't develop algorithms in isolation. I drive end-to-end solutions from requirements definition through architecture, implementation, integration, and production validation. At Sinikaari, the OptiSense platform redesign demonstrates this. We took a legacy signal conditioning architecture that was underperforming on key noise metrics and delivered a complete rearchitecture that achieved major SNR improvements while simultaneously reducing computational overhead. That kind of transformation requires genuine technical capability and the ability to coordinate across multiple engineering disciplines under real delivery pressure.

What specifically draws me to Kaikuvaara is the instrumentation focus. Building precision measurement instruments that must perform reliably in demanding conditions is engineering at its most consequential. There is no room for signal processing that works in simulation but fails when it matters. That alignment between high technical standards and real-world deployment rigour is exactly where my experience applies best.

I am committed to building engineering foundations that scale. Every solution I deliver is architected for long-term maintainability, not just immediate performance targets. When I hand work off to production engineering, it works, it is documented, and the next engineer who touches it can understand what is happening without guesswork.

Currently based in Oulu with no relocation required. I know the Kaikuvaara reputation well from the local engineering community -- serious engineering, precision instrumentation, high standards. That is the environment where my delivery orientation and technical depth create the most value.

Looking forward to discussing how I can contribute to Kaikuvaara's engineering roadmap.

Olli Makinen

extraction_contract.task: You are the extraction step of a candidate-screening support tool. For the one candidate in this task, read the CV and cover letter in full and classify, for EACH of the 12 requirements listed, exactly one status from this fixed vocabulary: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated. This is extraction, not evaluation -- you are locating and quoting what the text says, never judging whether the candidate is good enough.

status_definitions.evidence_found: The text gives a concrete, specific example of the requirement (a named project, employer, tool, or role detail) -- not just a keyword or a bare assertion.
status_definitions.claim_only: The requirement is asserted (e.g. listed as a skill, or claimed in a sentence) but with no concrete project, employer, or detail backing it up.
status_definitions.contradiction: Two statements in the application -- CV vs CV, letter vs letter, or CV vs letter -- cannot both be true at once about this requirement (e.g. a degree conferral date that is later than a job that required the degree; a claimed leadership title alongside a work-history entry that describes an individual-contributor role for the same employer and period). Quote both conflicting statements. Do not decide which statement is correct or resolve the conflict -- record that it exists.
status_definitions.not_stated: The text does not explicitly and unambiguously address the requirement, under any name for it, canonical or otherwise.

extraction_contract.refuse_to_guess_rule: REFUSE TO GUESS. If the requirement is not explicitly and unambiguously addressed in the text, the status is not_stated -- full stop. Never infer a requirement from a related or similar-sounding skill, a job title alone, general seniority, years of experience, or the prestige of an employer or university. A candidate whose job title was 'Senior RF Engineer' has NOT thereby evidenced hands-on RF measurement work unless the text itself describes that work. Where the text describes substantive work in different words from the requirement's own name, quote what the text actually says and let the quoted substance speak; what a description in adjacent vocabulary amounts to is a judgement call for the human recruiter, not something this extraction step resolves by guessing in either direction. When genuinely unsure between two statuses, choose the more conservative one (not_stated over claim_only, claim_only over evidence_found) and say so in the line's note.
extraction_contract.no_verdict_rule: This tool never ranks, scores, shortlists, rejects, or recommends a candidate, and never characterises the candidate as a whole. Do not use words or phrases like recommend, reject, shortlist, rank, top candidate, best, worst, strong candidate, weak candidate, good fit, poor fit, hire, do not hire, suitable, unsuitable, pass, advance, or any other language that compares this candidate to others or states what should happen to their application. State only what the text shows, per requirement. The recruiter decides; this output is preparation, not a decision.
extraction_contract.citation_rule: Every evidence_found, claim_only, or contradiction line must carry a VERBATIM quote: copied character-for-character from the CV or cover letter text given to you (leading/trailing whitespace may be trimmed, but do not paraphrase, summarise, correct, translate, or combine separate sentences). Tag every quote with its source: 'cv' or 'cover_letter'. A quote that cannot be found verbatim in the source document will fail citation verification and be reported as invented evidence -- when in doubt, quote a shorter, exact fragment rather than a paraphrase.
extraction_contract.ask_in_screening_rule: For EVERY must-have requirement (category 'must_have') whose status you set to not_stated, add one entry to the top-level ask_in_screening list: a plain, neutral, single-sentence question the recruiter could ask in a screening call to find out. Do not add ask_in_screening entries for desirable or constraint requirements, and do not add one for a must-have that is not not_stated. Questions must be neutral fact-finding, never leading and never implying a verdict (e.g. 'Can you describe your hands-on RF measurement experience, if any?' -- not 'Do you actually have RF experience, since your CV doesn't show it?').

return_format.description: Return a single JSON object for this one candidate (when extraction runs in a batch of 8, return a JSON array of 8 such objects, one per candidate, in the same order as the batch's `tasks` list).

schema.candidate_id: string, must match the task's candidate_id

requirements.status: one of: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated

lines.quote: verbatim quote from the application text (see citation_rule)

requirements.note: string or null -- required and must explain the conflict without resolving it when status is 'contradiction'; optional free-text otherwise (e.g. to flag a conservative-status judgement call under refuse_to_guess_rule)

return_format.note: The `requirements` array must contain exactly one entry per requirement given in this task, in the same order, covering all 12 requirement ids.
